contradictions.detail: The listing states 65,199 mi, but Carfax records 65,249 mi at a 09/24/2026 service, after the dealer acquired the car. The difference is small and consistent with a stale ad figure; confirm the current odometer reading.

documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is present: VIN, a Carfax with a guaranteed clean brand section, and a price stated to include all dealer fees. The maintenance half is thin: Carfax line items only, no invoices, none of the model-critical evidence, and no reported service entries for six years (2019–2025).

condition.rationale: No fault is stated. The photos show a clean, unworn tan interior and good paint with minor lower rear-bumper scuffs. Bore, IMS, cooling, top and underside condition are all unproven, and the recent history (no-start, airbag sensor, A/C recharge) leaves questions open.

price_value.rationale: $25,740 is about 10% below the $28,756 fair-value mid and below the active S peers ($28,195–$31,800). This is offset by the unknown cooling/IMS/bore status and a six-year service gap. The car also passed through an auction in 08/2026, so the dealer markup is unknown.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual and under the $27,000 ceiling, but above the $10,000–$19,000 ideal band. The 3.4 M97 carries the highest bore-scoring risk, which undercuts the 'reliable bridge' requirement until it is borescoped. Resale in 6–24 months is good for a manual S.

logistics.rationale: Indiana, about 1,945 mi from Carmel. It is a dealer car, so an independent Porsche PPI is plausible, but access is not stated. CA registration needs a smog check on arrival.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A manual Boxster S with sand-beige leather and 19-inch wheels is a desirable core spec. Black exterior is the soft end of the market. No PASM, Sport Chrono or hardtop is evidenced, and the shifter appears non-original.

ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders for scoring, especially bank 2 (cylinders 4–6)
Durametric/PIWIS: fault memory, cam deviation values and over-rev counts by range
Cold-start listen for rattle or ticking, plus smoke on startup (AOS)
Cut the oil filter or send an oil sample, given the service gap
Cooling system pressure test, water pump play/weep, expansion tank crust, front radiator and condenser corrosion
Check the A/C system for leaks, given the 2026 recharge
Underside corrosion inspection after the Minnesota years, plus RMS/bellhousing for drips
Cycle the top fully, check drains and footwell or under-seat moisture, and confirm the airbag light is out
Clutch engagement height and DMF judder, plus shifter installation if aftermarket
Front control arm and coffin-arm bushings, top mounts, and tire date codes
what_would_change_verdict: A clean borescope plus clean scan data (no significant over-revs, cam deviation in spec) would move condition and mission fit up materially.
Receipts for cooling-system work, or a benign Porsche Minneapolis inspection report, would raise documentation and condition.
Bore scoring, an active coolant or A/C condenser leak, or a recurring no-start fault would move it down sharply.
A dealer refusal of an independent PPI before deposit would move it down.
evidence.mission_note: A manual 3.4 Boxster S fits the enthusiast brief and sits under the $27,000 ceiling, though above the ideal band. As a bridge it depends entirely on proving the M97 bores and cooling system are sound.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax establishes a 2008 Boxster S manual with clean DMV brands, no reported accidents, a consistent odometer trail and five previous owners, the last of whom held it for nearly ten years in Minnesota. It also shows no reported service entries for six years (10/2019–11/2025). That gap was followed by a pre-sale cluster: a Porsche dealer inspection, a no-start check with battery, an airbag sensor replacement, an A/C recharge, and failed private listings ending in an 08/2026 auction sale to this dealer. The photos show a clean tan interior and good black paint, with minor lower rear-bumper scuffs and a likely non-original shifter. None of the model-critical evidence is present: no borescope, IMS documentation, scan data, cooling receipts or top video. The asking price is about 10% below the fair-value mid, but the M97's bore and cooling status remain open. The mileage discrepancy between listing and Carfax is about 50 miles and appears to be a stale ad figure.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer for the 09/24/2026 Jon Fricker invoice and the 11/2025 Porsche Minneapolis inspection results, and get written agreement to an independent Porsche-specialist PPI with borescope and Durametric scan before any deposit.
